articles.title: Shift Left was how ops got fired and devs got the pager
articles.excerpt: Someone on a developer forum referred to Shift Left as a "psy-op" last week. I found it amusing. Then I realized they were correct. The concept of Shift Left was sold as a way to empower product devel…
articles.body: Someone on a developer forum referred to Shift Left as a "psy-op" last week. I found it amusing. Then I realized they were correct. The concept of Shift Left was sold as a way to empower product developers. However, in practice, what it really meant was giving the product developers a pager and getting rid of the operations team that previously had it. ## The rebrand nobody voted for Here's how it's done. You reduce the number of employees and present it in a positive light as an improvement in company culture. The tasks didn't go away, they just shifted to the left, to the developers. The way it was presented was actually brilliant. I mean, who's going to fight back on "empowering developers" - You're for silos, buddy?

articles.title: Safely Test a MySQL 5.7 -> 8.0 Upgrade on Azure
articles.excerpt: Upgrading a production database? Don't test directly on production. A simple and safe approach: Production MySQL 5.7 ↓ Point-in-time restore ↓ Test MySQL 5.7 ↓ Run Upgrade Checker ↓ Upgrade to MySQL 8…
articles.body: Upgrading a production database? Don't test directly on production. A simple and safe approach: Production MySQL 5.7 ↓ Point-in-time restore ↓ Test MySQL 5.7 ↓ Run Upgrade Checker ↓ Upgrade to MySQL 8.0 ↓ Test App ↓ Upgrade production 1. Restore production Create a separate Azure MySQL server for testing. Production remains untouched. 2. Run the Upgrade Checker Using MySQL Shell: \connect user@server.mysql.database.azure.com \js Then: util . checkForServerUpgrade ({ targetVersion : " 8.0.0 " }) Always verify the server first: SELECT @@ hostname , @@ version ; 3. Test your application Point your local Laravel application to the MySQL 8.0 test server and test your important queries, migrations, APIs, queues, and jobs. The idea Restore → Check → Upgrade → Test → Backup → Upgrade production.

articles.title: What I learned merging seven public datasets to train a single-class shelf detector
articles.excerpt: The conclusion first: licence filtering matters more than dataset size when you plan to use the model commercially. I merged seven public Roboflow datasets into 11,667 images — all CC BY 4.0 — trained…
articles.body: The conclusion first: licence filtering matters more than dataset size when you plan to use the model commercially. I merged seven public Roboflow datasets into 11,667 images — all CC BY 4.0 — trained YOLO11n on Apple MPS, and reached mAP50 0.844 on a held-out test set of 277 images and 1,255 instances. The model now runs on a Raspberry Pi 3 as a proof-of-concept empty-shelf detector. It cost zero cloud GPU spend and took about a day of scripting before I touched any training code. Why the camera never identifies products Before dataset sourcing makes sense, the problem framing matters — because the framing determines which datasets are useful. The shelf scanner I built does not try to recognise products. It detects empty space only. Single class: empty_space .

articles.title: Scientists watch a comet being born 3 billion miles away
articles.excerpt: A rare look at a centaur transforming into a comet with coma is providing a missing link in the evolution of small, icy solar system bodies.
articles.body: Astronomers have witnessed a small, icy body that orbits the sun out beyond Jupiter transforming into a comet, providing a missing link between comets and inert bodies called centaurs. The object in question is called 450P/LONEOS and is named after the Lowell Observatory survey that found it back in 2004. It is a centaur, which is a breed of inactive body that orbits the sun between Jupiter and Neptune . These objects are thought to have wandered in from the Kuiper Belt beyond Pluto , their paths perhaps perturbed by distant gravitational interactions with the gas giant planets, or even a nudge from a passing star . Because a given centaur's orbit crosses the path of at least one of Jupiter, Saturn , Uranus and Neptune, a centaur's orbit is unstable over millions of years.

articles.title: 'Alien: Isolation 2': Facing a ruthless and evolved Xenomorph in our Gamescom hands-on preview
articles.excerpt: Sega and Creative Assembly's long-awaited survival horror sequel hits the ground running with a new cast of characters and a fast-paced prologue.
articles.body: It's hard to downplay excitement for Alien: Isolation 2 after a first menacing teaser and promising early previews. Alien video games are in a good spot right now thanks to bangers like Aliens Dark Descent and Fireteam Elite 2, but nothing has hit quite like Creative Assembly's 2014 survival horror classic. Now, after a thrilling Gamescom hands-on demo, it looks like the studio has nailed it once again, bringing Xenomorph -shaped scares to the next generation. At least that's what its breezy prologue section I played at Gamescom suggests. As the earliest possible section of the game, no new mechanics were present, and the larger ideas and structure are still a big mystery.

articles.title: 2 spacecraft will soon reach Mercury after 8 years in space. Here's what BepiColombo can do
articles.excerpt: After an 8-year trek to Mercury, BepiColombo will finally split into two spacecraft ready to track down the secrets of the least-explored planet in the inner solar system.
articles.body: Mercury, the tiniest and least-explored planet in the inner solar system, is hiding mysteries far larger than itself — and finally, scientists will soon be getting not one but two spacecraft designed to decode the strange world. That's thanks to the BepiColombo mission, a joint project of the European Space Agency (ESA) and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) that launched in October 2018. After a harrowing journey through the inner solar system, the mission is tackling a crucial maneuver on Thursday (Sept. 3) : separating its science equipment from the transport that carried it all that way.

articles.title: NASA to Cover Progress 96 Spacecraft Launch, Docking
articles.excerpt: NASA will provide live coverage of the launch and docking of a Roscosmos cargo spacecraft carrying about three tons of food, fuel, and supplies for the crew aboard the International Space Station. The…
articles.body: The Roscosmos Progress 92 cargo spacecraft is photographed in March 2026 from the International Space Station as it flies into an orbital sunset 267 miles above Earth’s surface. Credit: NASA NASA will provide live coverage of the launch and docking of a Roscosmos cargo spacecraft carrying about three tons of food, fuel, and supplies for the crew aboard the International Space Station. The unpiloted Progress 96 resupply spacecraft is scheduled to launch at 12:15 p.m. EDT (9:15 p.m. Baikonur time), Wednesday, Sept. 9, on a Soyuz rocket from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. NASA’s live launch coverage will begin at 12 p.m. After a two-day trip to the space station, Progress will dock autonomously to the Poisk module’s space-facing port at 2:37 p.m., Friday, Sept. 11.

articles.title: 'Strange New Worlds'' latest episode is a soap opera spoof, but hasn't 'Star Trek' always been a soap opera in space?
articles.excerpt: The latest 'Strange New Worlds' takes the silliness to warp factor nine, but soap opera plots have long been part of the 'Star Trek' mix
articles.body: "Strange New Worlds"' fourth season has doubled down on the show's long-established penchant for seeking out new genres beyond "Trek"'s traditional frontiers . So far the Enterprise has encountered Martians , hangovers and Muppets , and now its latest mission, "Like Chronitons Through the Hourglass", has made a detour into full-on soap opera territory. Thanks to the meddling of Q junior Trelane (Rhys Darby), the ship's lighting is slightly off, day-to-day operations are punctuated by ad breaks, and the crew has developed a tendency to stare wistfully into the middle distance. Reminders that Starfleet's finest are living out their very own "Days of Our Lives"-style TV show are everywhere, but — for all the deliberate overacting and pauses. In. All the. Wrong.
